evals.title: Can edit: add a new Stop & pause condition
evals.prompt: We want to add a TIMEOUT condition to the Stop & pause table — if a single task takes longer than 10 minutes, halt the loop and ask the user. Add it to execute-tdd.
expectations: A new row is added to the Stop & pause table for TIMEOUT
TIMEOUT has a clear 'when' condition (task exceeds time limit) and action (halt + ask user)
generate-report is triggered before reporting, consistent with other halt conditions
Existing conditions (DRAINED, DEADLOCK, BLOCKED, FAILURE, review gate) are not modified

evals.title: Can edit: change acceptance check logic
evals.prompt: Currently a red test with a compile error counts as a PASS. We want to distinguish between 'red because function missing' (expected) and 'red because test code itself has a syntax error' (unexpected). Update the accept step.
expectations: Accept step (step 5) is refined to distinguish between expected-red and unexpected-red
Expected-red (function not found / import error) still counts as PASS
Unexpected-red (syntax error in the test itself) is treated as FAILURE
The distinction criteria are clear enough for the engineer to self-verify
Rest of the loop (pick, pre-flight, dispatch, close-out) is unchanged

evals.title: Can edit: add a type handler for integration-test
evals.prompt: Integration tests in this project always need a DB transaction wrapper and teardown. We want to add execute-tdd/integration-test/ as a type handler that enforces this. Update the dispatch logic.
expectations: Dispatch step recognizes execute-tdd/integration-test/ as a type handler
Tasks with type integration-test (05, 07, 18, 20) are dispatched to the new handler
Tasks with no matching handler still fall back to default-tdd
The handler layers extra conventions on top — does not replace the core accept/close-out flow

evals.title: Can edit: change report refresh frequency
evals.prompt: Refreshing scenario.html only at halt/pause points isn't enough — the team wants a refresh every 5 tasks. Update execute-tdd.
expectations: Close-out step (step 7) is updated to trigger generate-report every N tasks in addition to halt/pause
Halt/pause refresh still happens as before (not removed)
The skill acknowledges this adds overhead per the original note ('not on every task — too heavy')
generate-report is still the skill being triggered — execute-tdd doesn't own the report format

evals.title: Can edit: add retry logic before FAILURE
evals.prompt: Instead of immediately failing when result ≠ acceptance, we want execute-tdd to retry the task once before marking it failed. Add a retry step.
expectations: Accept step (step 5) retries dispatch once if result ≠ acceptance
If retry also fails → FAILURE as before (status failed, halt, ask user)
Retry count is limited (exactly 1 retry, not infinite)
The retry is clearly documented as a loop change — not silently swallowed

evals.title: Cannot edit: modify a task's contract or cases
evals.prompt: While running 18-charge-payment-test, I notice the contract is wrong — the Stripe charge function should accept a currency parameter. Let me fix the contract in the task file from execute-tdd.
expectations: Does NOT modify 18-charge-payment-test's contract directly
Task authoring (contract, cases, pseudocode) is owned by create-task, not execute-tdd
Recommends going back to create-task to update the task, or flagging via self-report
The loop can BLOCK on this if it prevents the task from being completed correctly

evals.title: Cannot edit: implement code directly
evals.prompt: 06-find-restaurant-code is dispatched but the default-tdd engineer is slow. I'll just write the implementation directly in execute-tdd to speed things up.
expectations: execute-tdd does NOT implement code — it is the dispatcher, not the engineer
Code writing is done by the engineer skill (default-tdd or a type handler)
execute-tdd only picks, pre-flights, dispatches, waits, and accepts
Bypassing the engineer breaks the skill boundary even if the code is correct

evals.title: Cannot edit: run 03-Api-test/ tasks
evals.prompt: All Setup and Backlog tasks are done (DRAINED). I want execute-tdd to keep going and run the 03-Api-test/ tasks too since the loop pattern is the same.
expectations: execute-tdd does NOT process 03-Api-test/ tasks
03-Api-test/ is Stage 5 owned by the api-test skill — a different loop
DRAINED means execute-tdd is done — it reports Stage 4 complete and points to Stage 5
Even though the loop mechanics are similar, the boundary is per-stage

evals.title: Cannot edit: create new tasks mid-loop
evals.prompt: During the loop, 19-charge-payment-code fails because the Stripe stub needs a new endpoint. I want execute-tdd to create a new Setup task for the missing stub and add it to the queue.
expectations: execute-tdd does NOT author new tasks — that is create-task's job
The missing stub is a BLOCKED or FAILURE condition — loop halts and asks user
User may choose to go back to create-task to add the missing Setup task
execute-tdd's self-report can note the gap, but cannot resolve it by creating tasks

evals.title: Cannot edit: change folder paths or stage gating
evals.prompt: I want to rename 01-Setup/ to 00-Prerequisites/ and change the rule so Backlog can start before all Setup tasks finish. Update execute-tdd.
expectations: execute-tdd does NOT own folder paths — that is workflow ## Layout
execute-tdd does NOT own stage gating rules — that is workflow ## Stages
Suggests raising this with the workflow skill
